column2: Whoever at some time rises from that hell obtains human birth, and is born there short-lived.
Goddess, one joined with sinful action, with violence and the like, hostile to all beings, is born short-lived.
By good action, goddess, free of killing living beings, with weapons laid down, without the rod, he never harms;
he neither kills, nor causes to kill, nor approves of one who kills; affectionate to all beings, as to himself so to others —
such a man, goddess, always attains godhood; he always eats joyfully the pleasures and enjoyments that come to him.
If then at some time he is born in the human world, this is the path of the long-lived, of the well-conducted, of good actions, declared by Brahma as release from violence to living beings.
Those of awakened intellect give foot-water or rinsing-water; those who with love do not salute the teacher with what is auspicious and agreeable,
who abide with greed joined to increased pride, who disrespect the honourable and insult elders —
such men, goddess, all go to hell. If those men rise from that hell,
then after many years they obtain birth in a despised family of Shvapakas, Pulkasas and the like, despised and senseless.
They are born in families, pained by teachers and elders. One who is not hypocritical or proud, who worships deities and guests,
honoured by the world, bowing, born with sweet speech, doing what is dear in all actions, always dear to all beings,
without hatred, fair-faced, smooth, always giving gentle speech, by welcome alone not harming any beings,
worshipping appropriately with hospitality first, giving the road to one who deserves the road, always worshipping the teacher,
devoted to receiving guests and honouring those who arrive — such a man, goddess, attains the path to heaven.
Then, obtaining human birth, he is born in a distinguished family; there he has vast pleasures, joined with all jewels,
a giver as fits to the worthy, devoted to the practice of dharma, esteemed by all beings, bowed to by all worlds.
A man always gets the fruit of his own action by himself. This dharma was told by me, declared by the Creator himself.
But one of fierce conduct, terrifying to all beings, who with hands or feet, rope or rod,
clods, posts or devices, harasses creatures, auspicious one, intent on harm with the idea of retaliation, and agitates them,
who approaches creatures always causing agitation — one of such character and conduct goes to hell.
If he should reach humanity by the turn of time, he is born in a family afflicted by many troubles, among the base.
Hated by the world, the lowest of men, by the fruits of actions done by himself — this, goddess, is to be known among humans, kinsmen and relatives.
Another, compassionate, regards all beings with a friendly eye, like a father, without enmity, with senses restrained.
He does not agitate beings nor kill, devoted to compassion, trustworthy to all creatures with controlled hands and feet.
Neither by rope nor rod nor clods nor weapon does he agitate beings, doer of good, devoted to compassion.
One of such character and conduct is born in heaven; there he lives joyfully in a divine abode like a god.
If at the exhaustion of heaven that mortal is born among humans, he is born with little effort and free of fear and prospers happily.
A man is always a sharer in happiness, effortless, without anxiety. This, goddess, is the path of the good, where there is no affliction.
These humans are seen skilled in reasoning and discarding, endowed with knowledge and wisdom, intelligent, skilled in matters.
Others, god, are dull-witted, devoid of knowledge and wisdom; by what ripening of action does a man become intelligent?
How does a man become of little wit, ill-eyed? Cut this doubt of mine, best of the bearers of all dharma.
Some men are born blind, god, others afflicted with disease, others seen as impotent; tell the cause there."

Those who daily ask Brahmins knowing the Veda, Siddhas and knowers of dharma about good and bad,
brahmapuran:225:47	avoiding inauspicious action and practising the auspicious, always obtain a heavenly goal and comfort in this world.
brahmapuran:225:48	If he reaches humanity, the intelligent one is born there, one for whom learning in accord with sacrifice and welfare arises.
brahmapuran:225:49	Those who cast an evil eye on others' wives become blind from birth by that evil nature.
brahmapuran:225:50	Those who see a naked woman with even a defiled mind become afflicted with disease here, the doers of evil deeds.
brahmapuran:225:51	The foolish, ill-conducted men who delight in intercourse in an improper womb, very dull-witted among men, reach impotence.
brahmapuran:225:52	Those who bind animals, those who violate the teacher's bed, and those who have promiscuous intercourse are born impotent men.
brahmapuran:225:53	What action is blameworthy and what is blameless: the man who does good obtains it, best of gods.
brahmapuran:225:54	One who seeks the better path and always asks the Brahmins, seeking dharma, desiring virtue, attains heaven.
brahmapuran:225:55	If at some time, goddess, he reaches humanity, the intelligent, endowed with concentration, the wise, is born there too.
brahmapuran:225:56	This, goddess, is the dharma of the good, to be followed, bringing prosperity, and was thus told by me always for men's welfare.
brahmapuran:225:57	Others of little knowledge, haters of dharma, do not wish to approach Brahmins who know the Veda.
brahmapuran:225:58	Some men are of vows, devoted to faith and self-control; others without vows, fallen from restraint, are like Rakshasas.
brahmapuran:225:59	Sacrificers, and others free of delusion — by what ripening of action do they become so here? Tell me.

The limits of scripture, worldly dharmas, formerly established, are followed by authority; they are seen to be of firm vows.
brahmapuran:225:61	Those who, fallen under delusion, call adharma dharma, without vows, with limits lost, those men are Brahma-Rakshasas.
brahmapuran:225:62	Men who are born here from effort made by time, without oblation, without vashat, become the lowest of men.
brahmapuran:225:63	This ocean of dharma, goddess, with good and bad for men, has been explained by me to cut all your doubts.
The leader of all beings, bowed to by all beings, of this lord of gods and of the higher work,
who is always the embodiment of Brahman and the refuge of Brahman-sages: Brahma lives in his navel, and I am established in his body.
All the deities dwell comfortably in his body; that god is lotus-eyed, with Shri in his womb, dwelling with Shri,
bearing the Sharnga bow, discus and sword, banner of all the city-foes (?), with excellent good character, purity and self-control,
with valour, strength, body, appearance, height, vigour and wealth of uprightness,
endowed with mercy, beauty and strength, risen with all divine, wondrous-looking weapons,
thousand-eyed by yoga-maya, many-eyed, great-minded, praising friends in speech, dear to kin and relatives,
patient and free of boasting, that god is the giver of Brahman, remover of fear of the fearful, increaser of friends' joy,
refuge of all beings, devoted to protecting the wretched, learned, and prosperous, bowed to by all beings,
helper of those who have taken refuge, cause of fear to enemies, knowing policy, endowed with policy, speaker of Brahman, sense-conquered.
For the sake of the gods' existence, joined with supreme intelligence, in the auspicious Prajapati path, in human dharma refined,
Govinda will be born in the line of the great-souled Manu: Manu's son is Amsha, then Antardhaman;
of Antardhaman, Havirdhaman, the blameless Prajapati; Havirdhaman's son, Brahmins, will be Prachinabarhis.
He will have ten sons headed by Prachetas, and Daksha son of Prachetas will be the Prajapati here.
Daksha's daughter Aditi; from Aditya, Manu; from Manu's line, Ila and Sudyumna will be.
From Budha, Pururavas; from him Ayu will be; Nahusha will be from him, and Yayati his son;
from him Yadu, of great being; from him Kroshtu; Kroshtu's great son will be Vrijinivan.
From Vrijinivan will be Ushangu, unconquered; Ushangu's son will be Shura, and Chitraratha.
His younger son will be named Shura; in the line of those of renowned valour, endowed with conduct and virtue,
sacrificers and pure, best of Brahmins, that Shura, best of Kshatriyas, of great valour and great fame,
will beget a son increasing the extent of his own line, giver of honour, famed as Vasudeva, also Anakadundubhi.
His son will be four-armed Vasudeva, giver, honourer of Brahmins, become Brahman, dear to Brahmins.
That Yadava will free all the bound kings, and, having conquered King Jarasandha in a mountain cave,
he will be rich in all the jewels of kings; he, valiant, will be unobstructed on earth also by valour,
endowed with prowess, king of all kings, the hero, the lord, living at Dvaraka as a compact body,
will protect the goddess Earth, having conquered the evil-minded. Approaching him, you, with Brahmins and excellent honours,
should worship him duly like eternal Brahma. Whoever wishes to see me and Brahma the Grandfather
should see the revered, mighty Vasudeva. When he is seen, I am seen; there is no deliberation here.
Know, rich in austerity, that Vasudeva is the Grandfather. He with whom the lotus-eyed one is pleased —
for him the host of gods, with Brahma first, will be pleased. A man in the world who takes refuge in Keshava,
for him there will be fame, renown and heaven; he will be a teacher of dharmas directly, and righteous.
That lord of gods, Achyuta, is always to be bowed to by the knowers of dharma; dharma will always be, when that all-pervading one is worshipped.
That god of great brilliance, desiring the welfare of creatures, for dharma, tiger among men, created ten million sages;
created by him by that procedure, they stay on Mount Gandhamadana, led by Sanatkumara, joined with austerity.
Therefore that eloquent knower of dharma is to be bowed to, best of Brahmins; honoured, he honours; honoured, he returns honour.
Seen, he sees daily; resorted to, he gives refuge; worshipped, he always worships: that god, best of Brahmins.
Thus the supreme austerity of that blameless Vishnu, the great primal god, is always the conduct of good persons.
Worshipped constantly in the world even by the gods, eternal; with fitting fearlessness, taking refuge in him, devoted followers —
by deed, mind and speech he is always to be bowed to by the twice-born; approaching with effort, the son of Devaki should be seen.
This is the path ordained by me, best of sages; having seen him, lord of all gods, the best of gods are seen.
That god, the great Varaha, grandfather of all the worlds, I too always bow to, the lord of the world.
And there the three will be seen, no doubt: all of us gods live in his body.
His elder brother, shining like a heap of white mountain, will be known as Bala with the plough, the earth-bearer.
Three-headed, that god is seen as Ananta, the lord, by whose valour Suparna, the mighty son of Kashyapa,
could not see the end of the god, the Supreme Self; and that Shesha roams with supreme joy,
living within, embracing the earth with his coils. This Vishnu is Ananta, the revered earth-bearer.
Who is Rama is Hrishikesha Achyuta, supporter of all the earth; those two tigers among men, divine, of divine valour,
to be seen and honoured, bearing discus and plough. This favour has been told by me to you, rich in austerity, holy; therefore you should worship the best of the Yadus with effort."
Therefore listen, sages, to what you ask me, sinless ones; I shall tell in brief the course of those great-souled ones.
Having given up the human body, the seat of disease, impermanent, joined with old age and death, like a water bubble,
foul-smelling of flesh and blood, full of faeces and urine and the like, a post of bones, impure, with sinews, skin and veins,
in a vehicle going at will, sounding with divine Gandharva music, bright as the young sun, wreathed with nets of little bells,
sung to by Gandharvas, adorned with Apsarases, they go separately to the dwellings of the world-guardians.
Having enjoyed for the measure of a manvantara separately, their separate abodes adorned with all enjoyments,
then they go to the world of the atmosphere, giving all happiness; having enjoyed excellent pleasures there for ten manvantaras, Brahmins,
the Vaishnavas go from there to the world of Gandharvas, Brahmins; having enjoyed lovely pleasures there for twenty manvantaras,
they go, well honoured, from there to the Sun's world; having enjoyed very divine pleasures there for thirty manvantaras,
from there those Brahmins go to the moon's world, giving happiness, endowed with forty manvantaras' worth of virtue;
having enjoyed auspicious pleasures for a time, free of old age and death, from there to the world of the stars, adorned with vehicles,
they go, best of sages, adorned with all virtues; having enjoyed desired pleasures for fifty manvantaras,
from there those Brahmins go to the very rare world of the gods; having enjoyed very rare pleasures there for sixty manvantaras,
pleasures of many kinds, Brahmins, joined with eight hymns of the Rig, they then go to Shakra's world, honoured by the gods;
having enjoyed a time of seventy manvantaras there, high and low divine pleasures increasing the mind's delight,
from there they go to the unsurpassed world of Prajapati; having enjoyed desired pleasures there, joined with the qualities of all desires,
for eighty manvantaras of time giving all happiness, from there those Vaishnava Brahmins go to the Grandfather's world;
having played there for ninety manvantaras, happily, they come here again in the foremost family of Brahmins,
born as yogis, Brahmins, masters of the meaning of Veda and scripture. Thus having enjoyed desired pleasures in all worlds,
they come here and go again higher and higher in order. In each birth they, best of Brahmins, for a hundred years
enjoy desired pleasures and then go to another world. When their ten births are thus fulfilled in order,
then they go from Brahma's world to Hari's divine world; having gone there and enjoyed imperishable pleasures endowed with all virtues,
free of birth and death for a hundred manvantaras, they afterwards go to the abode of Varaha, best of Brahmins.
With divine bodies, earringed, huge-bodied, very mighty, they play there, best of Brahmins, taking a four-armed form.
For ten thousand ten-millions of years, best of Brahmins, they stay in the eternal state, bowed to by all gods.
